intro: Speaking in public: opening a talk, moving from point to point, stressing what matters and closing.
p.exposición.consejo: It is feminine and comes from «exponer». It is also an art show: «una exposición de fotos».
p.a continuación.consejo: It announces the next part: «a continuación, veremos…». It is written as three words.
p.por lo que se refiere a.consejo: A noun follows: «por lo que se refiere a los precios». It is formal.
p.respecto a.consejo: A noun follows: «respecto a los jóvenes». It is similar to «en cuanto a».
p.por otra parte.consejo: It adds another idea. It is written as three words and usually goes between commas.
p.tener en cuenta.consejo: It is «tener en cuenta», not «tener cuenta». A noun or «que» follows: «hay que tener en cuenta que…».
p.especialmente.consejo: It comes from «especial» plus «-mente». It highlights an important case.
p.concretamente.consejo: It comes from «concreto» plus «-mente». It serves to go from the general to an exact example.
p.como dijo.consejo: The name of the speaker and the quotation in quotation marks follow. «Dijo» is from «decir».
p.citar.consejo: You quote with quotation marks: «como dijo…». It also means to arrange a meeting with someone.
p.para finalizar.consejo: It announces the end of the talk. You can equally say «para acabar» or «para terminar».
p.resumiendo.consejo: It is the gerund of «resumir». It is used just before the final idea.
p.público.consejo: It has an accent on the ú: «el público». Without the accent, «publico» is a verb: «yo publico».
p.diapositiva.consejo: It is feminine: «una diapositiva». Each slide usually carries a single idea.
b1.texto:
**1. Opening.** Catch attention with a question and announce your plan:

- **¿Sabían ustedes que**…?
- **Hoy voy a hablarles de**…
- **En primer lugar**, explicaré… **A continuación**, veremos…

**2. Moving on.**

- **Por lo que se refiere a** los precios… / **Respecto a**… / **En cuanto a**…
- **Por otra parte**…

**3. Stressing.**

- **Hay que tener en cuenta que**…
- **Especialmente**, **concretamente**, **sobre todo**.
- Quoting: **Como dijo** Machado, «se hace camino al andar».

**4. Closing.**

- **Para finalizar**… / **Resumiendo**… / **En conclusión**…
- **Muchas gracias por su atención. ¿Alguna pregunta?**

The audience is addressed as **ustedes**, and each **diapositiva** carries a single idea.
b2.f0.texto: How do I open the talk?
b2.f1.texto: Start with a question for the audience.
b2.f2.texto: Did you know that we sleep almost a third of our lives?
b2.f3.texto: Very good, now announce the plan.
b2.f4.texto: Next, we will look at sleep habits.
b2.f5.texto: As far as adults are concerned, quote the doctors.
b2.f6.texto: Doctors recommend between seven and eight hours.
b2.f7.texto: We must take young people into account.
b2.f8.texto: The problem especially affects young people.
b2.f9.texto: To finish, sum up your idea in one sentence.
b4.texto:
These markers organise a talk:

- **Opening**: **hoy voy a hablarles de**…, **en primer lugar**, **a continuación**.
- **Moving on**: **por lo que se refiere a** + noun, **respecto a** + noun, **por otra parte**.
- **Stressing**: **hay que tener en cuenta que** + indicative; **especialmente**, **concretamente**.
- **Quoting**: **como dijo** + name, and the quotation in quotation marks.
- **Closing**: **para finalizar**, **resumiendo**.
b4.e0.texto: Today I am going to talk to you about our sleep habits.
b4.e1.texto: Regarding young people, the problem is bigger.
b4.e2.texto: To finish, I will sum up my main ideas.
b5.f0.texto: The hall is in half-light and smells of varnished wood and freshly made coffee.
b5.f1.texto: Irene steps onto the platform with her notes squeezed in her left hand.
b5.f2.texto: A white light falls over her and gently warms her face.
b5.f3.texto: On the screen at the back, the first slide shines with enormous letters.
b5.f4.texto: The audience keeps silent and waits with their eyes fixed on her.
b5.f5.texto: Irene takes a breath, smiles and begins in a clear voice.
b5.f6.texto: Her words float over the heads like small sheets of paper.
b5.f7.texto: Little by little, the nervousness dissolves in the warmth of the hall.
b5.f8.texto: In the third row, a girl draws stars in her notebook and looks up now and then.
b5.f9.texto: When she finishes, a long applause fills the hall like a summer rain.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: it announces what comes next.
b6.o2.refuerzo: That is said at the end, to close.
b6.pregunta: Which phrase announces the next part?
b7.frase: Hay que tener en ____ que los precios han subido.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «tener en cuenta» is the expression.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Cuento» is a story; the expression is «en cuenta».
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Tener en mente» exists, but it does not fit here.
b8.frase: Ahora quisiera pasar a hablarles de otro tema
b8.traduccion: Now I would like to move on to talk to you about another subject
b9.o0.refuerzo: That adds another point, it does not narrow one down.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Yes: it moves from the general to one exact case.
b9.pregunta: Which word points to one exact case?
b10.frase: Dormir bien no es un lujo, ____ una necesidad.
b10.o0.refuerzo: «Pero» adds a contrast; after «no» you need «sino».
b10.o1.refuerzo: Yes: «no es un lujo, sino una necesidad».
b10.o2.refuerzo: «Si no» is a condition; here it is one word: «sino».
b12.o1.refuerzo: Yes: it introduces a quotation from someone else.
b12.o2.refuerzo: To change topic you use «respecto a» or «por otra parte».
b12.pregunta: What does «Como dijo…» do in a talk?
p.abro.consejo: Starts with «a». The b sounds soft between vowels.
p.sabían.consejo: «sabían» is the imperfect of «saber». The accent is not written.
p.dormimos.consejo: «dormir» changes o to ue, but here o stays: «dormimos».
p.anuncia.consejo: Used for announcing news or a plan to others.
p.veremos.consejo: Future of «ver». The v sounds like b.
p.hábitos.consejo: Things we do again and again, like «hábitos de sueño», sleep habits.
p.refiere.consejo: «Por lo que se refiere a» means as far as ... is concerned.
p.adultos.consejo: Its opposite is «niños», children. Here it is used as a noun.
p.médicos.consejo: The stress is on ME. The c before i sounds like k.
p.recomiendan.consejo: «recomendar» changes e to ie. It means to advise.
p.afecta.consejo: «afectar» means to have an effect on someone or something.
p.resume.consejo: «resumir» means to shorten to the main points.
p.hablarles.consejo: «les» attaches to the infinitive: «hablarles», to talk to them.
p.resumiré.consejo: The -ré ending is the future: I will.
p.ideas.consejo: Plural of «idea». The two vowels are in separate syllables.
p.barnizada.consejo: From «barniz», varnish. It describes a shiny wooden surface.
p.estrado.consejo: A raised platform where a speaker stands.
p.apretadas.consejo: From «apretar», to squeeze. It agrees with «notas».
p.mirada.consejo: From «mirar», to look. The way you look at someone.
p.fija.consejo: Describes a steady look. The j sounds like h.
p.flotan.consejo: «flotar» means to float, to stay on the surface.
p.cabezas.consejo: Plural of «cabeza». The v-like b sound is not in this word.
p.aplauso.consejo: From «aplaudir», to clap. The au is one syllable.
p.tema.consejo: The subject of a talk or text. A common word for topic.
p.lujo.consejo: The j sounds like h. Its opposite is «necesidad».
p.necesidad.consejo: From «necesitar». Ends in -dad, like many abstract nouns.
